content:
Facts: Deceased donated usufruct rights to some heirs; pretermitted heirs challenged the deed as prohibited inheritance agreement or sought reduction for infringement of legitimate share.
Legal Framework: Prohibited inheritance agreements (Art. 458 Civil Code); action for reduction (Art. 553-564 Civil Code); reserved portions (Art. 536-564 Civil Code).
Interpretative Issues: Whether a donation of usufruct that affects the future estate constitutes a prohibited inheritance agreement; whether such donation infringes the reserved portion of legitimate heirs.
Legal Principles: A donation of usufruct capable of directly and immediately producing legal effects does not constitute a prohibited inheritance agreement despite affecting the future estate. The consequential effect on inheritance is a normal result of any dispositive act. For reduction actions, the reserved portion must be calculated on the estate formed by remaining assets plus fictitiously reunited donations. The donation violates reserved portions only when its value exceeds the disposable portion.
